examples.problem_statement: Evaluate 64.46 − 28.77 and give the answer correct to 1 decimal place

solution.operation: Set up the subtraction vertically, aligning decimal points
solution.description: Proper alignment of decimal points ensures accurate subtraction of corresponding place values
In the hundredths column 6 is smaller than 7, so a ten is borrowed from the tenths column and 16 minus 7 is taken instead, leaving 9.
The tenths digit has already given up a ten, so it now reads 3; since 3 is smaller than 7 another ten is borrowed, this time from the ones column.
The ones digit has already given up a one, so it now reads 3; being smaller than 8 it borrows in turn from the tens column.
The tens digit has lent one away and now reads 5, which is larger than 2, so this last column subtracts directly with no further borrowing.

solution.operation: Combine results and place decimal point
solution.description: Read the four column results back in order and set the decimal point under the aligned points of the original numbers to get 35.69.
The question asks for one decimal place, and the digit just past that place is 9, so the tenths digit 6 is rounded up to 7.

Collect the two terms that are being taken away, 59.826 and 79.66, into a single negative total in the same way.
Subtract the grouped negative total from the grouped positive total, padding 351.14 to three decimal places so the columns line up, which gives 211.654.

{'point': 'Borrowing is required when a top digit is smaller than the bottom digit in a column.'}

{'point': 'Always round final answers to the specified precision (significant figures or decimal places).'}
{'point': 'Note: When multiplying decimals, count total decimal places in factors to correctly place the decimal point in the product.'}

examples.problem_statement: The following set of data refers to the amount of money in £s taken by a news vendor for 6 days. Determine the mean, median and modal values of the set {27.90, 34.70, 54.40, 18.92, 47.60, 39.68}

solution.description: Rank the six daily takings from smallest to largest; the mean does not need this order but the median is defined by position, so the ranking is done once up front.
Set up the mean as the sum of all six amounts divided by six, writing the six values into the numerator.
Build the sum by running total rather than in one go, adding one amount at a time so a slip can be caught at the line where it happened; the total reaches 223.20.
Divide the total 223.20 by the six days to get a mean of 37.20 pounds.
Turn to the median: with an even count of six there is no single central term, so the rule averages the third and fourth terms of the ranked list.
Read those two terms off the list ranked in step 1: the third is 34.70 and the fourth is 39.68.
Average the two central terms, 34.70 and 39.68, to get a median of 37.19 pounds.
Finally look for the mode, the value occurring most often; every one of the six takings is different, so this set has no mode.
